title: Manchester United Fume Over Yoro Red Card as Liverpool Defeat Exposes Cracks
body:
Mauricio Pochettino was furious about Leny Yoro's red card in Manchester United's defeat to Liverpool [S1]. He also felt that Dominik Szoboszlai's opening goal should not have stood, which keeps the argument alive beyond the dismissal [S1].

Manchester United have notified the FA that they intend to appeal the red card [S2]. Sky Sports has also asked why the Szoboszlai free-kick was not ruled out, so the debate covers the goal as well as the sending-off [S1].

The league form shows why every point now matters. Over their last five league matches, Manchester United have no wins, two draws and three defeats, collecting 2 points while scoring 5 and conceding 14 [ST1]. Liverpool, across the same stretch, have four wins and one defeat, with 12 points, 11 scored and 3 conceded [ST2]. Those numbers point to a sustained slide, not one bad afternoon.

This is exactly the kind of blow that exposes a thin bench. When a side is already leaking goals, a sending-off turns a hard afternoon into a longer problem, and the manager needs answers quickly because the table does not wait for explanations.

The Touchline Take: fight the appeal, then fix the defending, because the next month will show whether this is a blip or a spiral.
